title: Unauthenticated /v1/register (and every non-partner route) reads an unlimited body into memory: remote memory DoS. The round-3 body-limit fix only covered partners.mjs
description: Commit 28842a1 added hono bodyLimit, but only to the routes in partners.mjs. server.mjs has no global body limit, and @hono/node-server imposes none. /v1/register is anonymous and calls `await c.req.json()` before it checks the join key, so it buffers the whole request, converts it to a string and parses it. The only guard in front of it is the X-Forwarded-For rate limit, and the client can spoof that header (see the separate finding). Member routes do the same after authentication: PUT /v1/figures/:id reads `c.req.arrayBuffer()` (line 458) and only then checks the 2 MB cap; /v1/posts calls parseBody (line 383) before checking the size of each photo; /v1/links, the parts routes and the others call c.req.json() with no limit; /v1/admin/import (line 600) reads the upload with no size or decompression limit.
failure_scenario: An anonymous internet client sends POST /v1/register with a 300-600 MB body (Content-Type can be text/plain, so a malicious web page can make visitors' browsers send it with no preflight). Each request drives the hub to about 1.3 GB RSS. Several at once exhaust the container's memory, and the hub is OOM-killed for every shop. The join key is not needed.
suggested_fix: Register a global limit before any route: `app.use('*', bodyLimit({ maxSize: 64*1024 }))`. Give larger per-route limits where needed: posts about 12 x 3 MB plus overhead, figures 2 MB, datasets and import as admin-configured and counted as the body streams. Keep /v1/register at a few KB. Check Content-Length first and use bodyLimit for chunked bodies, as partners.mjs already does.
evidence:
Own hub on :6417. Before: VmRSS 72516 kB. One 300 MB body to /v1/register (invalid join key) -> `status 403 {"error":"That join key isn't right..."}`, then VmHWM 1304968 kB. One 600 MB body -> `status 500`, log `code: 'ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG'`, VmHWM 1336780 kB. No authentication was used. The code reads the body first and checks the key after:
`const { joinKey, name, contact } = await c.req.json();` (line 126), before `same(sha(String(joinKey)), sha(expected))` (line 128).
verifier_notes:
confirmed: The code matches the report. server.mjs has no global bodyLimit, and @hono/node-server 2.1.1 sets no default limit (a grep of its dist finds no body limit). /v1/register is anonymous and calls `await c.req.json()` (line 126) before checking the join key (line 128). The only guard in front of it is the per-XFF allow() at line 125, which caps the request rate but not the size or concurrency of each request. Round 3 (28842a1) added bodyLimit only inside partners.mjs (`small` and `message`); its commit message scopes it to "Partner routes". Every other route is unbounded: PUT /v1/figures reads arrayBuffer() before its 2 MB check (458-459), /v1/posts runs parseBody before its per-photo checks (383-396), /links, /parts, /market and others use c.req.json(), and admin /import has no limit. Because an unauthenticated request can drive the hub's memory to several times the body size, a few parallel requests from anyone on the internet can OOM the one shared hub. I rate it high, not medium, because it needs no authentication; the impact is availability only, since installs keep local copies and resync later.
confirmed: Accurate to the code. server.mjs has no global bodyLimit; the round-3 fix (28842a1) added bodyLimit only in partners.mjs. /v1/register is anonymous and calls await c.req.json() at line 126 BEFORE the join-key check at line 128, so the whole body is buffered and parsed before any auth. The only guard is allow('register:${ip}',10) keyed on the spoofable x-forwarded-for header (line 124). @hono/node-server@2.1.1 imposes no default limit. Member/admin routes are unbounded too: /v1/posts parseBody (383), PUT /v1/figures/:id arrayBuffer then cap (458-459), admin /import raw.body (600), and various c.req.json() routes. Unauthenticated remote memory-exhaustion DoS that OOM-kills the shared hub for all shops on a small Railway/home deployment. Availability only (not data compromise), so high rather than critical; kept the reviewer's rating.

title: Brute-force rate limits keyed on spoofable X-Forwarded-For (join-key guessing on /v1/register)
description: The only brute-force protection on the community join key is `allow(register:${ip}, 10/hr)` where `ip = c.req.header("x-forwarded-for")?.split(",")[0]`. The hub trusts the first X-Forwarded-For token unconditionally (there is no TRUST_PROXY gate like the bench login limiter has). A client can send its own X-Forwarded-For header; on a hosted hub behind a proxy that prepends/passes the header, the attacker-chosen value is taken as the key, so rotating it gives unlimited attempts. The join key is a shared community secret (admin-settable, min 8 chars via /v1/admin/join-key), so an install-wide weak key becomes online-brute-forceable, granting full community membership (read all shared notes/links/marketplace, post spam, place orders). The public partner-join route has the same pattern (partners.mjs:142-143, pjoin:${ip}), though partner codes are high-entropy so less exposed.
failure_scenario: An attacker repeatedly POSTs /v1/register with guessed join keys, sending a different X-Forwarded-For (e.g. 10.9.1.1, 10.9.2.1, …) on each request. The register limiter never trips, so the attacker can grind the join key at full network rate and, on success, gets a valid installKey.
suggested_fix: Only trust X-Forwarded-For when running behind a known proxy (gate on an env flag as the bench does with TRUST_PROXY), and take the correct hop, not the first client-supplied token; otherwise key the limiter on the socket remote address. Add a global cap on join-key failures independent of client IP.
evidence: src/server.mjs:124-128. Reproduced on a private hub: 12 rapid POSTs from one IP returned 403,403,…,429,429 (limited at 11), but 12 POSTs each with a rotating `X-Forwarded-For: 10.9.$i.1` all returned 403 (never 429), and the correct key then succeeded: `{"installId":"63668e22…","installKey":"shk_7_NYZm4…"}`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Accurate. The register limiter keys on `x-forwarded-for`.split(',')[0] with no trusted-proxy gate, so a direct client, or one behind a proxy that appends to the header (nginx $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for style), controls the key and gets unlimited join-key guesses. Keys made with the admin page's 'Make a new one' are about 80 bits and safe. But JOIN_KEY from the environment has no minimum length and .env.example gives no advice on making one, and the admin PUT only requires 8 characters, so weak human-chosen keys are realistic. A correct guess gives full community membership, not other members' private partner or order data, and the admin can block the install. Related detail: clients with no XFF all share one 'register:local' bucket, so on a direct deployment an attacker can use up the 10 per hour and block legitimate joins. A limiter that is fully bypassable, on the only secret gating membership, with impact that depends on a weak key: medium.

title: Hub write budget shared across all companies on a multi-company install (one tech can deny all hub features to other tenants)
description: writeLimit() keys the 300/hr write budget on the installId. On a hosted multi-company StitchBench (PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS deployment) every company shares one hub connection and therefore one installId (there is a single HubState row, id=1, in the bench). So all companies draw from the same 300-writes/hour bucket, and any signed-in user of any company can exhaust it. "Sync now" (syncCommunityHub) calls reportUsageNextSync() then pushUsage(), which unconditionally sends 2 POST /v1/usage writes per sync; a low-privilege TECH can press it (or replay the server action) ~150 times to consume the whole install's budget, after which every other company's hub writes (creating/updating listings, accepting/paying/shipping orders, adding/fixing manual links, sharing notes) fail with 429 for up to an hour.
failure_scenario: On a hosted install holding shops A and B, a TECH at shop B repeatedly triggers Sync now (each = 2 hub writes). After ~150 syncs the install hits write:${installId} 300/hr. Shop A's owner then cannot list a part or act on a marketplace order: every hub write returns 'Too many changes in the last hour.'
suggested_fix: Either give each company its own install/key on a multi-company hosted install, or track and rate-limit hub usage per company (shopId) on the bench before calling the hub, and/or raise/scope the hub budget per member. At minimum, stop 'Sync now' from spending write budget on usage reporting on every click (respect the hourly usage-push guard).
evidence: src/server.mjs:161-163 `allow(write:${c.get("install").id}, 300)`; single install per bench (src/lib/hub.ts HubState id:1). Reproduced: captured shop B tech's Sync-now server action and replayed it in a loop; bench log then repeatedly logged `community hub usage: Too many changes in the last hour.` and shop A's owner listing attempt surfaced the toast `Too many changes in the last hour. Try again later.`
verifier_notes: confirmed: Accurate. writeLimit (src/server.mjs:161-163) allows 300 writes per hour per installId. The bench has one HubState row (id=1, hubState() in src/lib/hub.ts:58) that every company on the install shares; requireInstallAdmin's own comment says the hub connection belongs to the whole install. syncCommunityHub (src/actions/hub.ts:38-42) needs only requireUser (any role, any company). It calls reportUsageNextSync(), which zeroes lastUsagePush, so every 'Sync now' ends with pushUsage() sending 2 POST /v1/usage, each counted by writeLimit (usage.mjs:26). addManualLink and other requireUser actions also spend the shared budget. About 150 syncs by one tech (on a hosted app with ALLOW_SIGNUP, even a newly signed-up shop) fill the bucket, and every other company's hub writes (listings, order steps, manual links, notes) then fail with 429 for up to an hour, repeatably. Reads keep working. Cross-tenant DoS that needs a login: medium.

title: Hub figure store is first-writer-wins with no replace or delete: any member can permanently poison the figures every install shows
description: PUT /v1/figures/:id accepts any 24-hex id from any member and inserts with `ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING`, then returns {ok:true} even when the upload was discarded. Figure ids are deterministic: sha1(sourcePath|page|box) over data that ships with every installer (seed-data/factory_settings.json) and is sent to every user in page props. So a malicious member can compute the ids for all ~14k settings and upload wrong or offensive images before the honest shops do. Nothing can replace or delete them: there is no hub endpoint or admin action for figures. Installs that don't have their own copy show the hub's (/api/figures/[id] falls back to hubPicture), and the bench caches that copy in HubFigure forever (src/lib/hub.ts:700-707 never re-fetches once data is set).
failure_scenario: Mallory registers with the join key, computes figureId for every factory setting from the shipped JSON, and PUTs a misleading image for each. Every member install without the manual now shows Mallory's image under 'Show figure' for needle-bar height, timing and so on. When an honest bench later shares the real figure, the hub answers ok:true but keeps Mallory's, and there's no way to fix it short of editing the hub DB.
suggested_fix: Record the uploader (install_id is already stored) and let the original uploader or the hub admin replace or delete a figure, with an admin endpoint and admin.html control, and a changes-feed entry so benches drop their cached HubFigure.data. Return a distinct status (e.g. 409 or {kept:false}) when the upload is ignored. Consider letting the hub admin approve figures before they're served, or at least bounding per-member figure count and size.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The code matches the description. stitchhub/src/server.mjs:453-469 accepts any 24-hex id from any member, inserts with ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING, and returns {ok:true} even when the upload is discarded. No hub route updates or deletes figures: the admin routes are summary, join-key, discord-*, installs/:id/block, delete posts, links import, datasets, export and import. figures.install_id has no foreign key, so blocking a member leaves their figures in place. On the bench, hub.ts:700-707 keeps HubFigure.data forever once fetched. model-info marks a figure as stored when a HubFigure row exists, and manual-figure.tsx then shows the hub copy instead of drawing and saving its own, so installs that have the manual are affected too. Figure ids are sha1 of data that ships with the program (factory_settings.json) and is sent in page props. What limits the impact: the attacker needs a join key and must upload before an honest shop, so figures already on the hub are safe. Figures not yet uploaded, including those for new settings in an update, can be poisoned permanently and no one can correct them.

title: Deleting a note (by its author or by the admin) doesn't remove it: /v1/changes keeps sending its full title, body and photo list to every member, and its photos stay downloadable
description: DELETE /v1/posts/:id (line 430) and the admin DELETE (line 543) only set deleted=true and bump seq. /v1/changes (lines 224-240) still returns title, body, authorName and photo metadata for deleted posts. GET /v1/photos/:id (line 439) serves photos without checking whether the post is deleted. StitchBench discards deleted posts (savePost deletes locally), so the content is useless to honest installs but available to anyone who reads the API, including shops that join later (since=0).
failure_scenario: A tech shares a note that includes a customer's name, phone number or address, or a photo of a label. The owner deletes it (or the admin removes abusive or illegal content). Any member, or any shop that joins later, calls /v1/changes?since=0 and still gets the full text and photo ids, then downloads the photos. Moderation and retraction don't work.
suggested_fix: When a post is deleted, clear title/body/author_name (or return only {id, deleted:true} in /changes for deleted rows) and DELETE its photos rows in the same transaction. Make /v1/photos/:id join posts and return 404 when the post is deleted.
evidence: Own hub: B posted "Timing fix for Mrs Jane Doe 555-0100" with a photo, then DELETE -> {"ok":true}. Member A's /v1/changes?since=0 returned `{"deleted":true,"title":"Timing fix for Mrs Jane Doe 555-0100","body":"Customer Jane Doe, 12 Elm St, serial 12345678, paid cash","photos":[{"id":"592eab...","kind":"CONDITION","caption":"customer label",...}]}`, and GET /v1/photos/592eab... -> `200 image/png 27 bytes`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The member DELETE (430-437) and the admin DELETE (543-546) only set deleted=true and bump seq. /v1/changes (223-240) selects every column of posts and photos, with no filter on deleted. GET /v1/photos/:id (439-443) doesn't check the post. The bench drops deleted posts locally, but anyone reading the API can still see them, including shops that join later with since=0. Retraction by the author and admin moderation are both ineffective (the export carries deleted rows too). This is a privacy and moderation failure, so medium.
also_reported_as: code: src/server.mjs:226 Deleted notes are still sent in full (title, body, photo ids) to every member, and their photos are still served

title: Photos of a removed note are still served to every member
description: DELETE /v1/posts/:id (and admin DELETE /posts/:id) only sets posts.deleted = true. GET /v1/photos/:id reads `SELECT mime, data FROM photos WHERE id = $1` and never checks the post. Every install that synced the note before removal already has the photo ids from /v1/changes, so it can keep downloading them. The usual reason to remove a note is that a photo shows something it shouldn't, such as a customer's name label or serial number, which the README promises are never shared. Removal does not take that photo back. Photos of removed notes are also kept in every export.
failure_scenario: A tech shares a note with a photo that shows the customer's name tag, notices, and removes the note. Other installs drop the note locally, but any member who saw the photo id in an earlier sync can still GET /v1/photos/<id> and receive the image.
suggested_fix: Serve only photos of live posts: `SELECT ph.mime, ph.data FROM photos ph JOIN posts p ON p.id = ph.post_id WHERE ph.id = $1 AND NOT p.deleted`. Better still, delete (or null out the data of) the post's photo rows in the same statement that marks the post deleted.
evidence: On my hub: shop A posted a note with a photo, then DELETE /v1/posts/<id> returned `{"ok":true} 200`. Shop B's GET /v1/photos/3621c43f14bc4021a367768b still returned 200 with `\x89PNG...CUSTOMER-NAME-IN-PHOTO`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: DELETE /v1/posts/:id (server.mjs:431) only soft-deletes. GET /v1/photos/:id (server.mjs:440) never checks the post. The exposure is wider than the reviewer said: /v1/changes (server.mjs:224-239) returns deleted posts with their title, body and photo ids to every member, including installs that join after the removal. So any member can fetch the photos of a removed note, not only installs that synced before the removal. StitchBench fetches photos lazily (hub.ts:4 and 690-697), so many installs never held the bytes locally. Removed notes are also kept in exports. The precondition is member auth, so I kept it at medium.
also_reported_as: qa: src/server.mjs:439 Hub keeps serving photos of removed notes (and of removed listings) by id

title: Hub process crashes whenever Postgres drops an idle connection (no pool 'error' listener); unawaited notify() can also crash it
description: `new pg.Pool(...)` has no `pool.on('error', ...)` handler. When an idle pooled client gets an error (Postgres restart, managed-DB failover or maintenance, a proxy idle timeout, pg_terminate_backend), pg-pool re-emits it on the pool. With no listener, Node throws an unhandled 'error' event and the whole hub exits. The 1-second positions() interval from 28842a1 means there is almost always an idle client in the pool, so any DB restart takes the hub down. Railway's ON_FAILURE policy restarts it, but migrate() fails while the DB is still down. That crash-loop can use up Railway's restart retries and leave the hub down. A related cause: notify() (server.mjs:67) is called without await or .catch() at 6 places. If getSetting() rejects during a DB blip after a write, the rejection is unhandled, and Node 22 exits on unhandled rejections.
failure_scenario: Railway restarts the Postgres service for maintenance. Idle hub connections get FATAL 57P01, the pool emits 'error', and the hub process dies. Every in-flight upload and order action fails, and if the DB takes longer than the restart budget to come back, the hub stays down.
suggested_fix: Add `pool.on('error', (e) => console.error('db pool:', e.message))` in db.mjs; pg discards the broken client and the next query opens a new connection. Make notify() fully self-contained: wrap its body in try/catch, or call it as `notify(...).catch(() => {})`. Optionally add `process.on('unhandledRejection', ...)` logging as a backstop.
evidence:
Reproduced on my own hub: `select pg_terminate_backend(pid) from pg_stat_activity where datname='qa_hub_codecore' and state='idle'` gave `hub process 16029 is gone`. The log shows:
node:events:497
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
error: terminating connection due to administrator command
    at parseErrorMessage (.../pg-protocol/dist/parser.js:306:11)
verifier_notes: confirmed: db.mjs:6 creates pg.Pool with no 'error' listener. pg-pool re-emits errors from idle clients on the pool, so Node throws on the unhandled 'error' event and the process exits. The 1 s positions() interval (db.mjs:163) plus the 10 s idleTimeout mean an idle client is almost always in the pool, so any DB restart, failover or backend kill takes the hub down. notify() (server.mjs:67) awaits getSetting and is called without await or catch at 6 sites. A DB error there is an unhandled rejection, which also exits the process on Node 22. The restart policy (Railway ON_FAILURE, docker unless-stopped) usually brings it back. However, migrate() at startup fails while the DB is still down, so a longer DB outage can use up Railway's retries. That part was not demonstrated.

title: SSRF: the link checker (on by default) fetches member-supplied URLs on loopback, private and link-local addresses, follows redirects, and shows every member the internal HTTP status
description: validUrl (server.mjs:57-64) only checks for http/https. The checker (enabled unless LINK_CHECKER=off; .env.example leaves it on) sends HEAD, then a ranged GET, to every link URL with `redirect: "follow"`. It does no DNS or IP filtering and no port restriction. The result is stored in links.http_status and status and returned to every member in /v1/changes (linkOut httpStatus), which gives a status-code oracle. A member can re-probe on demand: editing the URL resets checked_at, and POST /v1/links/:id/report sets it to NULL, and the checker picks NULLs first within 60 s. StitchBench itself refuses to download hub links from private networks (fetchPublic in src/actions/hub.ts), but the hub has no such guard.
failure_scenario: A member adds links such as http://192.168.1.1/..., http://<service>.railway.internal/..., or http://127.0.0.1:<port>/..., or a public URL that redirects to one of them. Within a minute the hub sends HEAD/GET requests into its own network: the NAS, router, printers or the shop PC for a docker-compose hub, or other project services on Railway. The attacker reads the 200/404/403 results in /v1/changes to map internal services, and can trigger internal GET endpoints that have side effects.
suggested_fix: In probe(): resolve the host, reject loopback, RFC1918, link-local (169.254/16, fe80::/10), ULA, CGNAT, 0.0.0.0/8, multicast and *.internal. Connect to the vetted IP (a custom undici Agent `connect` lookup) so DNS rebinding cannot swap the address. Use `redirect: "manual"` and re-validate each hop, up to 5. Allow only ports 80 and 443. Consider applying the same check when a link is added so members get feedback. Reuse the logic of the bench's fetchPublic.
evidence:
Own hub on :6417 with the checker on, and a fake internal service on 127.0.0.1:6418 that logs requests:
`HEAD /admin/secret-exists "StitchHub-LinkChecker/1.0 ..."`
`HEAD /redirect` then `HEAD /admin/reboot?via=redirect` (redirect followed to the internal path)
Another member's /v1/changes then showed:
`http://127.0.0.1:6418/admin/secret-exists ok 200`
`http://127.0.0.1:6418/admin/nothing-here unchecked 404`
`http://127.0.0.1:6418/redirect ok 204`
verifier_notes: confirmed: validUrl (57-64) checks only the protocol. The checker runs unless LINK_CHECKER=off (.env.example leaves it empty, so it is on). probe() uses `redirect: "follow"` with no host, IP or port filtering. The result (status and http_status) goes to every member through linkOut in /v1/changes. POST /v1/links/:id/report sets checked_at=NULL for any link id, with no write limit, so a member can re-probe on demand. A member can therefore map the hub's internal network (the NAS or LAN of a docker-compose hub, *.railway.internal on Railway) and trigger internal GET/HEAD requests, including through a redirect. It is blind (status code only), HEAD or ranged GET, and needs a join-key member, so medium.
also_reported_as: code: src/checker.mjs:11 Link checker fetches any member-supplied URL, including loopback and private addresses, and publishes the HTTP status to all members

title: README's hub-move promise has no StitchBench flow: re-joining at a new address creates a new install and loses the shop's listings, orders and notes
description: The README says: 'After an import, members keep working with their existing keys once they point StitchBench at the new address.' transfer.mjs keeps install key hashes and seqs for that purpose. StitchBench has no way to change the hub URL while keeping the key. joinHub (stitchbench src/lib/hub.ts:245-279) always POSTs /v1/register at a new URL and stores the new installId/installKey, and it refuses outright when the shop has active partner links. desktop/join-hub.mjs does the same. After a move to a new address (e.g. a new *.up.railway.app), the shop's old install id still owns its listings, open orders (seller or buyer), notes ('mine') and partner links on the imported hub. The shop's new install can't see /v1/orders for them, can't edit or remove its listings, and can't remove its notes.
failure_scenario: The admin moves the hub from app-old.up.railway.app to app-new.up.railway.app and imports the export. A seller re-joins at the new address as instructed. Its 3 active listings and 2 accepted-but-unshipped orders belong to the old install id, so it can no longer mark them paid or shipped. A shop with partner links is told to 'End those partnerships before moving to another hub', which the export was meant to preserve.
suggested_fix: Add a 'hub moved' action in StitchBench (Settings → Community hub → Change address). It should validate the new URL with GET /v1/me using the existing key, confirm that the installId matches, then update only hubState.url and keep all cursors. Until then, correct the README to say moves must keep the same address (custom domain) or members lose ownership of their marketplace items.
evidence: stitchbench src/lib/hub.ts:254-262: `if (cur?.installKey && (await db.partnerLink.count({ where: { status: "ACTIVE" } }))) throw new UserError("...End those partnerships before moving to another hub."); const r = await reach(`${base}/v1/register`, ...)`. hubState.url is written only by joinHub, the partner join and join-hub.mjs, and all of them register a new install. No action updates url while keeping installKey.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The code matches the claim. The README (stitchhub README.md:55-59) says members keep their keys once they 'point StitchBench at the new address', but no StitchBench path changes hubState.url while keeping installKey. Only four places write url: joinHub (src/lib/hub.ts:255-272), the partner join (src/lib/partners.ts:219), desktop/join-hub.mjs, and leaveHub, which nulls it. The first three all register a new install and reset every cursor to 0. The hub ties ownership to install_id: market.mjs:356 serves orders only by buyer/seller_install_id, partners.mjs:160/198 filter by repair/retail_install_id, and posts 'mine' plus DELETE /posts use install_id. So after a move to a new address, the new install loses its listings, orders and notes. It is worse for a shop with active partner links. joinHub refuses (hub.ts:254), leaveHub refuses (hub.ts:278), and endPartnership (partners.ts:229-231) needs hubFetch to reach the old, now dead URL. That shop has no UI path at all. It also means 28842a1's 'keep change numbers' work only helps moves that keep the same address. Medium: an uncommon flow, but a documented one that loses ownership of data.
also_reported_as: security: README.md:59 The README says members keep their keys after a hub move by pointing StitchBench at the new address, but StitchBench can't do that: re-joining always registers a new install

title: The hub export is not a consistent snapshot: an export taken while members are active can contain rows whose parents are missing, and the all-or-nothing import then fails with a generic error
description: lines() pages each table with separate autocommit q() calls, streaming lazily as the client reads, and reads tables one after another in FK order. It never takes one snapshot. Rows written during the export can be missing from a parent table that was already exported but present in a child table exported later: posts->installs, photos->posts, link_revisions->links, order_events->orders, partner_messages->partner_links. importStream runs in a single transaction and aborts on the first FK violation. The admin only sees "Something went wrong on the hub." The README tells admins to "Download an export now and then and keep it somewhere safe", so those backups may not be restorable.
failure_scenario: The admin downloads a backup while a new shop joins and shares a note, and keeps the file. Later the hub is lost. Importing the backup fails: the post references an install that isn't in the file. Nothing is restored, and the error doesn't say why.
suggested_fix: Run the whole export on one pooled client inside `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` (read the meta sequences in the same transaction) and COMMIT when the generator finishes. Release the client on stream error or abort. Have the import report the table and line that failed (e.expose) and add an import round-trip test to test/smoke.mjs.
evidence: Own hub: export streamed with the reader paused after the first chunk. Meanwhile a new shop registered and posted. Result: `export rows: 8340 installs: 2 posts whose install is missing from the file: [['8e9888ce...','c74da08c...']]`. Importing into a fresh hub returned `{"error":"Something went wrong on the hub."}`. The log showed `insert or update on table "posts" violates foreign key constraint "posts_install_id_fkey" ... Key (install_id)=(c74da08c...) is not present in table "installs"`, and `select count(*) from links` was 0.
verifier_notes: confirmed: lines() (transfer.mjs:194-212) issues a separate autocommit pool query per 200-row page and table, and the generator is pulled lazily under stream backpressure, so it never takes one snapshot. Rows committed mid-export can appear in a child table while their parent was already paged past. FK constraints exist: posts.install_id -> installs, photos -> posts, link_revisions -> links, and others. importStream runs in one transaction and aborts on the first violation, and the admin sees only the generic 500 message. A slow admin download widens the window, and new links (revisions) or notes with photos commonly land in it. The README's periodic-backup advice therefore yields files that may not restore.
also_reported_as: code: src/transfer.mjs:109 Export is not a consistent snapshot: a backup taken while shops are active can be impossible to import (the whole import rolls back on a foreign-key violation)
code: src/transfer.mjs:109 Export loads 200 photo/figure rows per page into memory (about 4x the raw bytes in RSS)

title: Restoring an older export (or importing into a live hub) leaves installs' cursors ahead of the restored sequences: they silently skip every new note, link, part, listing, order and partner message numbered at or below their cursor
description: Round 3 (28842a1) keeps row seqs and sets change_seq and partner_messages_seq_seq to greatest(meta value, current value, max(seq)). That is correct only when the export was taken just before the import. Restoring a backup taken earlier sets the sequences to the backup's values, while installs have already synced past them (StitchBench keeps its cursor as long as the hub URL is unchanged). /v1/changes, /v1/orders and /v1/partners/messages never notice that `since` is beyond the current sequence value; they return nothing and `next=since`. Importing into a non-empty hub has the same effect: rows get older content with older seqs, and installs never see the rollback.
failure_scenario: Backup taken at changeSeq 4373. Later edits move installs to cursor 4376. The hub is restored from the backup at the same address. The next changes (new notes, link fixes, new orders, and partner messages such as repair status, estimates and settlements, which use a separate sequence with the same logic) take numbers 4374..4376. Every existing install skips them for good.
suggested_fix: In /v1/changes, /v1/orders and /v1/partners/messages, return `reset: true` when `since` is greater than the sequence's current last_value, and have the bench restart that cursor from 0 (its upserts are idempotent). Alternatively, store a random hub `generation` in settings, change it on every import, return it from /v1/me, and have the bench reset all cursors when it changes. A large setval jump on import is a weaker stopgap.
evidence: Own hubs: backup meta `"changeSeq":"4373"`. Three more links were added, and member B synced to cursor `4376`. The backup was imported into a fresh hub, then a member posted: `new note seq|4374`. B then polled: `member B polls since 4376 -> posts: 0 links: 0 next: 4376`, so the note was never delivered.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The import sets change_seq to greatest(meta.changeSeq, current, max(seq)) (transfer.mjs:268-277), and the partner sequence the same way. That is correct only for a fresh export. Restoring an older backup, which is the README's disaster-recovery path, rewinds the sequence below cursors the installs already hold. The bench keeps hubState.cursor unless it re-joins (hub.ts:635-655), and the hub never signals a reset. New changes numbered in the gap are skipped for good. Because the link checker bumps seq for every link it checks, a real backup trails live seq by thousands, so the gap is large. This is the round-3 "installs keep their place" fix working only for fresh exports, not for older backups. Less common flow, but silent data loss, so medium.

title: Importing into a hub that is already in use keeps old change numbers (regression from 28842a1): restored rows never reach installs, duplicate seqs make paging skip rows, and one matching URL aborts the whole import
description: Since 28842a1, a version-3 export row is inserted with its original seq (`kept`), and ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE also copies `seq = EXCLUDED.seq`. This is only correct when the target hub has never handed out change numbers. The admin page presents import as 'Rows with the same id are replaced', which covers restoring a backup into the live hub and loading an export into a hub that was already seeded or joined. In either case: (1) imported or replaced rows get seq values below the cursors installs already hold, so installs never receive them, and a row that was newer on the hub is reverted there while installs keep the newer copy (silent divergence). (2) Two rows can now share a seq across tables, and /v1/changes pages with `seq > since ... LIMIT n`, so a page boundary between equal seqs skips the second row. (3) links are upserted ON CONFLICT (id) only. If the target already has the same URL under another id (both hubs seeded from hub_links.json, or a member added it), the links_url_file unique index aborts the entire import. Before 28842a1, every imported row got nextval, so issues (1) and (2) did not exist.
failure_scenario: Hub B is in use, and member M has synced to cursor 8. The admin imports an export from hub A (rows seq 3-5). The import reports links 1, posts 2, but M's GET /v1/changes?since=8 returns nothing, so M never sees them. A fresh install paging with limit=1 receives one of the two seq-3 links, next=3, and never receives the other. After a member adds a link to B whose URL also exists in A, the next import attempt fails completely with a 500.
suggested_fix: At the start of importStream, check whether the target is untouched (change_seq is_called = false and all WITH_SEQ tables are empty). Keep row.seq only in that case. Otherwise assign nextval('change_seq') to every imported or updated row (after setval to greatest(meta.changeSeq, current)), so every install receives the imported state once. Apply the same rule to partner_messages. For links, resolve url/file_name conflicts explicitly (skip, or merge into the existing id) instead of letting the unique index abort the transaction, and say in the admin UI that import is meant for an empty hub.
evidence: Reproduced with two of my own hubs (6391 as A, 6393 as B). Import result `{"settings":1,"installs":2,"links":1,"link_revisions":2,"posts":2,"photos":31}`. Then `after import, since=8 -> links 0 posts 0 next 8`. DB: `links|race test|3` and `links|Hub2 H300 manual|3`. Paging: `page1 ['Hub2 H300 manual'] next 3 more True` then `page2 ['Hub2 H400 manual'] next 4`, so 'race test' was skipped. After adding https://example.com/dup-two.pdf on B and re-importing: `{"error":"Something went wrong on the hub."} 500`, log `constraint: 'links_url_file'`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: Since 28842a1, importStream keeps row.seq (transfer.mjs:159-166) and the upsert copies seq = EXCLUDED.seq. It never checks that the target has not handed out change numbers yet. In a target that is already in use (a live hub restored from a backup after vandalized link edits, or a hub that was seeded or tested first), imported or replaced rows get seqs below the cursors installs already hold, so installs never receive them. Before 28842a1 every imported row got nextval, so this is a regression. The same seq can also end up on rows in two tables, and /v1/changes pages with `seq > since ORDER BY seq LIMIT n`, which skips the second row at a page boundary. The admin confirm text ('Rows with the same id are replaced') invites this use. Part (3), the links_url_file abort, is real but existed before 28842a1 (ON CONFLICT (id) only).
